spec_family.name: Exterior Garage Door Prime and Paint
spec_family.description: EA-based spec for new construction exterior garage doors. Three substrate materials (steel/wood/carriage) with substrate-driven primer selection. Sectional door articulation requires leapfrog painting technique. Factory-primed steel STILL requires DTM primer (wax contamination). Bottom seal lifecycle management (remove/prop/reinstall). Door size (single/double) is primary EA rate modifier. Panel complexity (flush/raised_panel/carriage/windows) is secondary modifier. Door casing belongs to SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1.

includes: Complete exterior face of garage door assembly (all panels, recesses, window frame surrounds)
Panel edges at articulation joints (leapfrog painting technique)
Track and hardware masking (tracks, rollers, springs, cables, brackets)
Bottom seal management (remove or mask, prop during cure, reinstall after cure)
Driveway/apron protection (canvas drops — NOT poly sheeting)
Substrate-driven surface preparation (steel: wax removal + degloss; wood: sand + fill + tannin spot; carriage: mixed-material prep)
Substrate-driven primer application (DTM for steel, acrylic for wood, alkyd stain-blocker for tannin wood, bonding for carriage composites)
Two finish coats with leapfrog technique (standard or premium acrylic latex)
Six-side sealing for wood doors per DASMA TDS #162
Articulation test (door opens/closes freely after painting)
Balance check (safety quality gate — spring adjustment is not scope)

excludes.item: Garage door casing/trim prep, prime, and paint

excludes.route_to: PROHIBITED — introduces orange peel on metal door faces
EXCLUDED — garage doors are visible from street, not economy-appropriate
EXCLUDED — utility surface, not architectural showcase like entry doors

configuration_dimensions.description: Quality tier controlling pace, scrutiny level, intercoat sanding, and defect tolerance.
configuration_dimensions.notes: QT3=standard (production pace, 6-foot visual, no intercoat sand). QT4=premium (slower pace, raking light at 3 feet, intercoat sand 220-grit, premium materials). QT2 excluded — visible from street. QT5 excluded — utility surface. Narrow 2-tier range reflects functional character of garage doors.

configuration_dimensions.description: Garage door substrate material — drives primer system, prep protocol, and failure mode profile.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Steel: wax removal + degloss + DTM primer (factory-primed steel STILL needs DTM due to wax). Wood: sand + fill + acrylic primer + six-side seal per DASMA TDS #162. Carriage: mixed-material prep (steel base + composite overlays) + DTM on base + bonding primer on overlays. Per-door capture for mixed-substrate projects.

configuration_dimensions.description: Panel complexity classification — secondary cost driver after door size.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Flush = baseline (continuous spray). Raised_panel = +10% (brush work in recesses). Carriage = +30% (meticulous masking, multi-tone cutting, overlay detail). Windows is additive time (independent of panel type). Windows can coexist with any panel type.
No locked-in default. Semi-gloss is most common for garage doors. Gloss requires higher prep quality. All valid for this spec.

configuration_dimensions.description: Primary application technique for face coating.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Spray is primary for garage door faces (large flat panels, ideal for airless spray). Brush for panel recesses on raised-panel and carriage doors. Brush-only for small projects where spray setup is not justified. Roller is NOT valid — introduces orange peel on metal doors. Back-rolling AVOIDED on metal doors per Application Methods Doctrine.

paintable_items.name: Exterior garage door assembly
paintable_items.counting_rules: Each garage door assembly is 1 EA regardless of physical size. Door size (single or double) is captured as a modifier within EA. A door assembly includes all panels, recesses, window inserts (if present), and panel edges at articulation joints.
paintable_items.notes: Single paintable item. Does NOT include casing (SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1 scope), interior/garage-side face, weatherstripping, spring hardware, or tracks. Door size dimension (single/double) drives time per EA. Panel complexity dimension (flush/raised_panel/carriage/windows) drives detail time per EA. Substrate (steel/wood/carriage) drives primer and prep protocol.

variants.notes: Baseline scenario — single steel flush QT3 spray. Wax removal + degloss + DTM primer + 2 finish coats. No window masking. No brush recess work.
Standard spray on raised-panel steel. Adds brush recess work to spray face. 1.10x panel complexity modifier.
Standard spray on carriage-style. Meticulous overlay detail work. 1.30x panel complexity modifier. Carriage substrate adds bonding primer for composite overlays.
Any substrate with window inserts. Adds window masking zone. Additive time for window masking (+0.75-1.25 hrs).
Wood door QT3 spray. Adds sand + fill + acrylic primer + six-side seal per DASMA TDS #162. 1.15x substrate modifier.
Premium spray on steel flush. Intercoat sanding 220-grit. Premium acrylic enamel. 1.15x QT modifier.
Brush-only on steel flush. No siding masking needed (no spray overspray). Brush is ~2.5x spray time for face tasks. Used when spray is not feasible.

required_paintscope_inputs.description: Count of garage doors in scope. Each door assembly is 1 EA regardless of size.
Garage door substrate material — steel, wood, or carriage. Drives primer system, prep protocol, and failure mode profile.
Garage door size — single (8x7/9x7 ft, 56-63 SF) or double (16x7/18x7 ft, 112-126 SF). Primary rate modifier within EA counting.
Panel complexity — flush, raised_panel, carriage, or windows. Production rate modifier.
Boolean flag confirming new construction context. Always true for this NC spec.

required_paintscope_inputs.required_when: When application_method is spray (recommended for all methods)
required_paintscope_inputs.description: SF of driveway/apron surface within overspray/drip zone requiring protection.

valid_input_states.notes: Three NC-relevant substrate states. SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY is dominant for steel (~85%). SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD for wood panel doors. SS_EXT_BARE_METAL is rare in NC (factory primer damaged). Key difference from entry doors: factory-primed steel STILL needs DTM primer (wax contamination — no skip-prime path for garage doors).

output_state.notes: Output state varies by sheen. Semi-gloss is most common for garage doors.

SS_EXT_PRIMED_FACTORY.notes: Factory-primed steel STILL needs DTM primer. Factory primer is inadequate due to wax contamination. Wax removal + degloss required before DTM application.

SS_EXT_BARE_METAL.notes: Bare steel requires DTM primer. Rare in NC (factory primer damaged). CRITICAL: prime same day as surface prep.

SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD.notes: Acrylic primer for bare wood. For tannin-rich species (cedar, redwood, fir), supplement with SYS_EXT_GRDR_PRIMER_ALKYD_STAINBLOCK spot or full. Six-side seal mandatory per DASMA TDS #162.

material_systems.name: DTM Primer for Steel Garage Doors
material_systems.notes: Rust-inhibitive acrylic DTM primer. MANDATORY for ALL steel garage doors including factory-primed (wax contamination). Flash-rust resistant, flexible for thermal expansion.

material_systems.name: 100% Acrylic Exterior Primer for Wood Garage Doors
material_systems.notes: Standard 100% acrylic latex exterior primer. For non-tannin species (pine, fir, spruce). Supplement with alkyd stain-blocker for tannin-rich species.

material_systems.name: Alkyd Stain-Blocking Primer for Tannin-Rich Wood Garage Doors
material_systems.notes: Required for cedar, redwood, fir garage doors. Deep penetration, superior tannin blocking. May be spot-applied at knots or full-surface for severe tannin species.

material_systems.name: Bonding Primer for Carriage-Style Composite Overlays
material_systems.notes: Conditional — only needed when carriage overlays have glossy/sealed composite surfaces. Grips slick composite while providing tooth for topcoat.

material_systems.name: Standard Exterior Acrylic Latex for Garage Doors
material_systems.notes: Mid-grade 100% acrylic exterior latex. Works on all three substrates (steel, wood, carriage). LRV restriction: carriage/composite LRV > 55 (HARD STOP). Steel LRV > 30 recommended (IR-reflective below 30).

material_systems.name: Premium Exterior Acrylic Latex for Garage Doors
material_systems.notes: Premium 100% acrylic (SW Emerald, BM Aura). Superior UV resistance, self-cleaning technology, enhanced color retention.

modules.name: Garage Door Final Inspection & Bottom Seal Prop
modules.notes: Bottom seal prop (TSK_GRDR_BOTTOM_SEAL_PROP) is in FINISH_2 module (immediately after second coat). Final inspect module handles inspection, balance check, and touch-up.

production_summary.rate_basis: EA (each garage door assembly) — minutes per door, not SF/hr or LF/hr

ea_conversion.notes: Single door: 8x7 or 9x7 ft (56-63 SF). Double door: 16x7 or 18x7 ft (112-126 SF). Rates are minutes per door, with door_size modifier adjusting for doubles.

time_estimates_by_scenario.notes: Baseline — excludes driveway SF protection time. With typical driveway: ~5.3-5.8 hrs. Comprehensive task breakdown including full protection setup/cleanup.
1.85x single door time. Setup/cleanup has some fixed overhead.
Carriage adds brush detail work. QT4 adds intercoat sand + premium materials.
Wood adds six-side seal, grain management per DASMA TDS #162.

production_summary.worst_case_stack: Double (1.85) x carriage (1.30) x QT4 (1.15) x wood (1.15) = ~3.18x multiplicative + window additive. Environmental modifiers can push to ~4.55x, capped to 4.0x.

protection_zones_required.notes: Driveway/apron below garage door. Canvas drops or absorbent mats — NEVER standard poly (slippery safety hazard on hardscapes). Mandatory for spray and recommended for brush.
Siding panels flanking garage door opening. Pre-taped poly or masking film. Spray method only.
Window inserts in garage door panels. HDPE static-cling film. Only when windows present. Divided-lite adds significantly more time.
Weatherstripping contact surfaces along sides and top. Low-tack tape deep in channel. Paint destroys seal flexibility. NEVER paint weatherstripping.
Track, roller contact points, spring mechanism, cables, brackets. Must NOT be painted — causes binding. Mask from garage interior side.
Bottom weatherseal (astragal). Either remove before painting or mask. Prop door 2-4 inches during 24-48 hr cure. Dedicated management lifecycle: prep -> prop -> reinstall.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Garage door casing frames the opening. Different finish typically. SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1 scope. No cut-in tasks from this spec to casing — casing is trim spec's responsibility.
Siding-to-garage door junction: casing intervenes. No direct adjacency edge work. Siding masking (TSK_GRDR_SIDING_MASK) is protection task, not edge work.
Driveway below garage door. Non-painted protection target. No cut-in — driveway protection is zone-based.

site_condition_rules.affected_tasks: Spray application tasks and siding masking tasks
site_condition_rules.notes: High wind excludes spray tasks entirely — reschedule. Moderate wind adds overspray containment overhead. Especially critical for garage doors (large flat spray target).
Full sun compresses leapfrog working window. South/west-facing doors especially critical. Schedule early morning for sun-exposed doors.

site_condition_rules.affected_tasks: All prime and finish coat application tasks
site_condition_rules.notes: Cold (< 50F) slows cure, risks adhesion. Hot (> 90F) causes flash dry and lap marks. Steel doors heat up faster than wood — surface temp modifier is critical for steel.

adjacent_specs.relationship: Garage door casing/trim painting belongs to trim spec. This spec covers the door panel assembly only.
Entry door painting is completely separate. Different context prefix (XDOR vs GRDR), different PS keys. No shared EA count.

cross_spec_boundaries.cross_spec_protection_note: Driveway/apron protection is THIS spec's responsibility (overspray source is the garage door). Adjacent siding masking during garage door spray is also this spec's responsibility. Garage door trim/casing protection DURING SIDING SPRAY belongs to the siding spec.
deduplication_notes: Garage door CASING/TRIM painting belongs to SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1 — this spec covers door panel assembly only.
Driveway/apron protection IS this spec's responsibility — not the siding spec or trim spec.
Adjacent siding masking during garage door spray IS this spec's responsibility (overspray source is the garage door).
Garage door trim/casing protection DURING SIDING SPRAY is NOT this spec's responsibility — belongs to siding spec.
Entry door painting (SF_DOOR_EXT_NC_v1) is completely separate — different context prefix, PS keys, and EA counts.

round_configurations.description: 1 primer coat + 2 finish coats — standard NC sequence for ALL garage door substrates
round_configurations.notes: Single round configuration — ALL garage doors get primer + 2 finish. Unlike entry doors, factory-primed steel garage doors STILL need DTM primer because wax removal compromises factory primer reliability. No skip-prime path.

issues.description: Intercoat tasks use appears_in_tiers in SOP vs qt_conditional_tasks in production — different structural patterns, functionally equivalent.
Baseline ~4.8 hrs for single steel flush QT3 spray is comprehensive (includes 2.3 hrs setup/cleanup). Core painting is ~2.2 hrs, consistent with industry.
Driveway protection uses SF UOM while other protection tasks use EA — correct because driveway area varies independently of door count.

doctrine_checks_passed: THREADING-1 through THREADING-6 (task ID completeness, classification match, applies_when consistency, UOM match, task prefix, module prefix)
EXT-1 through EXT-7 (key namespace, substrate state, protection zone, site conditions, factor keys, modifier math, material state)
GRDR-1 through GRDR-8 (EA rates, leapfrog technique, bottom seal lifecycle, wax removal, DTM for all steel, wood six-side seal, QT range, articulation test)
COMPLETENESS-1 through COMPLETENESS-5 (protection zones, cross-spec boundaries, round configurations, module phase order, input declarations)

sequencing_notes.production_sequence: Setup -> Prep -> Prime -> Finish 1 -> Interstage -> Finish 2 -> Final Inspect -> Cleanup
sequencing_notes.protection_sequence: Driveway protection -> Siding masking (spray) -> Window masking (if present) -> Weatherstrip protection -> Track/hardware masking -> Bottom seal management -> Equipment setup -> Coating work -> Window unmask -> Weatherstrip unmask -> Track/hardware unmask -> Siding unmask -> Bottom seal reinstall (after 24-48 hr cure) -> Driveway teardown -> Articulation test -> Tool clean
sequencing_notes.leapfrog_sequence: Paint alternating panels (1,3,5 then 2,4,6) -> Open each joint to verify tack-free -> Paint adjacent panels -> Verify no bridged joints at articulation points
sequencing_notes.coat_sequence: Prep (substrate-driven) -> Prime (1 coat, ALL substrates including factory-primed) -> Finish coat 1 (leapfrog) -> Interstage (inspect, sand QT4, repair, dust) -> Finish coat 2 (leapfrog) -> Bottom seal prop -> Final inspect -> Touch up
sequencing_notes.key_prohibitions: NO roller application. NO back-rolling on metal doors. NO standard poly sheeting on driveway. NO painting on track/hardware/springs. NO skipping DTM primer on factory-primed steel. NO closing door on uncured bottom seal.

relationships.notes: First exterior garage door spec. Adjacent to trim spec (casing). No direct siding adjacency (casing intervenes). Key departures from exterior entry door spec: no fiberglass substrate, leapfrog technique, bottom seal lifecycle, wax removal, factory-primed steel still needs primer, QT3-QT4 only (2 tiers), door size modifier instead of complexity tiers, single round config.

change_log.author: SpecFactory
change_log.changes: Initial draft spec for exterior garage door prime and paint. First exterior garage door spec — EA-based single-item spec (ITM_GARAGE_DOOR) with 3 substrate materials (steel/wood/carriage), 4 panel complexities (flush/raised_panel/carriage/windows), 2 door sizes (single/double), 3 sheens (satin/semi-gloss/gloss), 2 application methods (spray/brush), QT3-QT4 quality tiers (QT2 and QT5 excluded). 46 tasks across 8 modules (26 binary, 16 qt_scaled, 2 qt_conditional). 6 material systems (4 primers + 2 finishes). 6 protection zones. 8 factor modifiers (4 spec-specific + 1 QT + 3 environmental). 1 round configuration (all substrates get prime + 2 finish). Context prefix GRDR. Key features: leapfrog technique for sectional doors, bottom seal lifecycle management, wax removal for steel, factory-primed steel still requires DTM primer, wood six-side seal per DASMA TDS #162, articulation test at cleanup, canvas-only driveway protection. QA result: pass (3 minor issues, 0 blockers).
